correctness.rationale: Identity T=R(theta h)/theta−(1−theta)I/theta makes all off-diagonals positive and identifies the diagonal criterion. For each state, regenerative holding/return cycle gives R_ii(s)=[1+q_i s(1−E exp(−H_i/s))]^{-1}. Because s(1−exp(−H/s)) increases strictly for H>0, R_ii falls from 1 to π_i, remaining above π_i for finite s. Taking the minimum gives one unique crossing for 0<theta<theta_c and no crossing for theta≥theta_c. Expanding to order 1/s gives c_i=(π_i² q_i/2)E H_i²; θ_c(θ_c−θ)h_c→min_{π_i=min π} c_i. θ=0 has Euler positivity cutoff 1/max q_i. Independently derived exact 3-cycle cutoff 1+√5 and complete 3-state cutoff 2 for theta=1/2, same π=(1/3,1/3,1/3); computations do not replace general regenerative proof.

value.rationale: A natural sharp positivity phase diagram for an entire class of probability-conserving discretizations, including nonreversible and nonnormal finite networks, with a generator-independent criterion from minimum stationary mass and a precise geometry-dependent near-critical return-time law. Separate finite cutoffs distinguish generators with identical stationary distributions.

final_claim: For every irreducible finite row Markov generator Q, the endpoint theta method T_{theta,h} is nonnegative for all h>0 iff theta≥1−min_i π_i. For theta below this boundary it has a unique sharp cutoff determined by min_i (I−theta hQ)^{-1}_{ii}=1−theta; as theta increases to the boundary the cutoff diverges with an explicit positive second-return-time moment coefficient.
limitations: Finite irreducible row-conservative Q only; applies to endpoint theta step, not stage positivity or higher-order RK families.
Generic finite cutoff is defined by a unique root, not claimed in radicals.
